summary: The study investigates the structural, electrical, and optical properties of Si-doped ZnO (SZO) films deposited by atomic layer deposition (ALD) using triethyzinc, tris(dimethylamino)silane, and H2O2 as precursors at 300 /C176C. The optimal Si concentration of 2.1 at% resulted in the lowest resistivity of 9.2 × 10^-4 X cm, with a carrier concentration of 4.3 × 10^20 cm^-3 and a Hall mobility of 15.8 cm^2/Vs. The optical bandgap initially increased with Si concentration but then decreased beyond 2.1 at%, attributed to the Burstein-Moss effect. The study highlights the potential of ALD for fabricating high-quality SZO films suitable for optoelectronic applications.
evidence: Abstract Si doped ZnO (SZO) films with various Si concentrations were deposited by atomic layer deposition at 300 /C176C using triethyzinc, tris(dimethylamino)silane and H2O2 as the precursors. The minimum resistivity of 9.2 9 10^-4 X cm, with a carrier concentration of 4.3 9 10^20 cm^-3 and a Hall mobility of 15.8 cm^2/Vs, was obtained for SZO film prepared with the Si concentration of 2.1 at%. The optical bandgap of SZO films initially increased from 3.25 to 3.55 eV with increasing of Si concentration to 2.1 at%, then decreased with further increase of Si concentration. The blue shift of band gap of SZO films with increasing carrier concentration can be explained by the Burstein-Moss (B-M) effects.
